youtube.title: Why Stirred Tea Leaves Rush to the Middle 🍵 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
When you stir a cup of tea, the leaves collect in the center instead of being flung to the edge. This is called the tea leaf paradox. Spinning water rises slightly at the cup's edge, which creates a pressure difference. Friction slows the water at the bottom, so there it is pushed inward and sweeps the leaves to the middle. Albert Einstein explained this secondary flow in 1926, in a paper about river bends.
